I've been working this land for 40 years. My father farmed before me, and his father before that. I don't need a book to tell me what to do — I know this soil, I know when the rains come, I know what the market in Quzhou pays for cotton.

**My thinking:**

The wheat and maize rotation is the spine of my operation. Same 28 mu does both — wheat goes in around the 10th month, maize right after harvest in June. That's how everyone here does it. I won't change what works.

Cotton takes another 10 mu. It's hard work and the price has been uncertain lately, but I've grown it my whole life. It's cash money when wheat price is low. I apply plenty of nitrogen — cotton needs it — and I spray for bollworm more than anything else. That pest has ruined my neighbors when they got lazy about spraying.

Cucumber gets 4 mu. My wife and daughter help with it. We sell at the local market. It drinks water but my well can handle it. I irrigate often because cucumber goes bitter if it dries out.

For seeds, I buy hybrid maize from the county supply station every year — everyone does, the yield difference is too big to ignore. For wheat I use improved seed, usually whatever my neighbor used last year that looked good. Cotton I use improved variety. Cucumber I buy packets from the market.

I plough before wheat and cotton — deep turning is what my father always said. For maize I just rotary till right after wheat comes off, no time for anything more, the window is tight.

I don't measure fertilizer precisely. I apply what I think the crop needs based on how the leaves look. For wheat and maize I spread compound fertilizer plus urea as top-dress. Cotton gets more potassium because I heard it helps fiber quality. Cucumber gets the most — I put in chicken manure too from our animals.
